simple.meaning: רָחַק (râchaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to widen (in any direction), i.e. (intransitively) recede or (transitively) remove (literally or figuratively, of place or relation).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 58 times across Genesis, Exodus, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges, and 10 more, beginning at Genesis 21:16. Its contexts include family line, flock, righteousness, city, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָחַק (H7368).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָחַק (râchaq) / H7368 is traced through Genesis 21:16, Genesis 44:4, Exodus 8:24, Exodus 23:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.
